entries.title: Azuremyst Isle
body: The larger of the two Azuremyst Isles, off Kalimdor's north-western coast: evergreens and purple flowers, lashed by arcane storms and wrapped in thunder and fog. Long ago it was a mountainous forest on the western edge of ancient Kalimdor. The night elves deliberately left it untamed, a hunting ground where beasts could feed and hunters trap the choicest prey, and when the Great Sundering tore it from the mainland, its plants and animals slowly adapted to island life.

Now it is home to the draenei. Their great ship, the Exodar, crashed into its western mountains, scattering power crystals across the island and changing the creatures that touched them. The survivors have made the wreck their city, and resolved to give their lives in defence of their new home.
sources: warcraft.wiki.gg: Azuremyst Isle (introduction, Early history, Geography)

entries.title: Ammen Vale
body: The eastern part of the island, cut off by the Crystalbrook River and sheltered by hills on every side. A section of the Exodar fell here in the crash, and the draenei who survived it have turned its wreck into a refuge.
The vale's purple fields are scattered with crystal fragments, and its lashers, moths and owlkin have been changed by the radiation leaking from the ship's broken power cores.

entries.title: The Crash Site
body: Where the largest piece of the Exodar to fall in Ammen Vale came to rest. The survivors woke here among the wreckage and the dead, and at once set about healing the injured and salvaging what they could, with no idea at first whether anyone else had lived.
Among the first to help them was a stranger: the pandaren Mojo Stormstout, who had been cataloguing the island's wildlife when the ship came down.

entries.title: Silverline Lake
body: A lake in south-eastern Ammen Vale that for centuries was a source of pure water for the vale's wildlife. One of the Exodar's crystal shards fell into it in the crash, and since then its waters have warped the creatures that drink from them.

entries.title: Nestlewood
body: The thickets and hills of southern Ammen Vale, home of the Nestlewood owlkin. When the Exodar broke up, the owlkin gathered up the strange pieces of the ship that fell among their nests.
The crystals' radiation has driven some of them mad. The draenei, unwilling to make enemies of the vale's people, have worked to protect the ones it has not yet touched.

entries.title: Shadow Ridge
body: A line of high, craggy hills in south-western Ammen Vale. Blood elves of the Sunhawk, the faction that sabotaged the Exodar's reactors, regrouped here after the crash under Surveyor Candress. They followed the draenei from Outland, and their master Sironas set them to survey the islands.

entries.title: Azure Watch
body: A forward outpost of the Hand of Argus, the draenei's military order, built after the crash between Ammen Vale and the Exodar. Its artificers raised the town from salvage, and one of the ship's escape pods became its inn.
Elekks did much of the work, carrying the building stone and timber the draenei needed. A steady stream of injured comes through, and its healers are rarely idle.

entries.title: Moongraze Woods
body: The forest around Azure Watch, grazed by moongraze stags. The draenei took to hunting them at once: they look much like the talbuk of Draenor, the favourite prey of draenei hunters on their old world.
Nightstalkers prowl the woods too, and some have swallowed the irradiated crystals, carrying the corruption deeper into the forest.

entries.title: Odesyus' Landing
body: A small Alliance outpost on the southern shore, little more than a campfire, a two-storey log wall and two ships moored offshore. Admiral Odesyus was forced to put in here when goblin stowaways stole his fleet's compass and charts.

Loggers, axemen and Stormwind marines make up its crew. One night the ghost of Edward Hanes, captain of the lost ship Lost Hope, appeared outside the admiral's tent to tell him the tale of the Bloodcurse.

entries.title: Geezle's Camp
body: A Venture Company camp near the island's south-eastern shore, named after its goblin boss, Geezle. The goblins came ashore hidden in the admiral's own holds, planning to strip-mine the Exodar's crystal wreckage and then steal the ships to carry it away.

entries.title: Traitor's Cove
body: A small beach on the eastern side of Silvermyst Isle, where the goblins met their secret contact among the admiral's own crew, and gave the place its name.

entries.title: Wrathscale Point
body: The ruins of a night elven city on the island's southern coast, older than the War of the Ancients, filled with ancient relics. The sea cave of Tides' Hollow beneath it was once part of the same city.
Naga of the Wrathscale have taken both, and their warlord, Sriss'tiz, has been gathering reinforcements from Nazjatar to conquer the islands.

entries.title: Bristlelimb Village
body: A small furbolg village in western Azuremyst, home of the Bristlelimb tribe. The Bristlelimb and the Stillpine have lived on the islands for centuries, and the Bristlelimb have now turned hostile and gone to war with their neighbours, carrying off Stillpine captives in cages.

entries.title: Stillpine Hold
body: The cave home of the Stillpine furbolgs in the north of the island. For centuries the tribe lived in relative peace with the island's creatures. They have mastered a rare skill: carving a totem in the likeness of an animal and using it to bond with a beast of that kind, without months of study.

The peace ended with the Exodar's fall, which the furbolgs call the crystal storm. Their old allies the Oomooroo owlkin, maddened by the crystals, drove them from their hold with a beast out of legend, the Kurken.

entries.title: Silting Shore
body: The north-western shoreline of Azuremyst, crowded with the huts of the Siltfin murlocs. The Stillpine always had a tenuous relationship with them, but never imagined the murlocs would dare to raid their food stores.

entries.title: Menagerie Wreckage
body: Wreckage on the north-eastern beaches where the Exodar's menagerie came down. The ship carried living specimens from Outland, and the crash broke open the cages of the ravagers, voracious insect-like predators that escaped into the forest and fell on the Stillpine hunters.

entries.title: Silvermyst Isle
body: A small island off Azuremyst's south-western coast, close enough to swim to. The night elves mostly abandoned the islands long ago for the mainland, but being so close to Teldrassil, a few stayed. The fisherman Cowlen and his family lived peacefully here among the owlkin for many years.
Crystal shards from the Exodar fell here too, and drove the Moonwing owlkin mad. A fire elemental named Hauteur, crazed by the crash, has made them worship him and burn effigies in his honour.

entries.title: The Sacred Grove
body: A well-hidden glade deep in north-western Ammen Vale, concealed by two mountains and thick trees and guarded by the Spirit of the Vale.
The spirit tells of a deeper wound left by the crash: the balance of the elements has been broken. The earth elementals have turned in rage on the other elements sent to calm them.

entries.title: Wildwind Peak and Emberglade
body: Wildwind Peak is the great mountain the Exodar crashed into. A cave near its summit holds a draenei shaman, and the lord of the island's air elementals speaks from the heights.
In the north-east, Emberglade is a burnt ring of trees where fire elementals dwell, home of the fire spirit Temper.

entries.title: Valaar's Berth
body: A dock outside the Exodar on the island's west coast. The night elven ship Elune's Blessing sails from here to Rut'theran Village, linking the draenei to Darnassus and the mainland, and a small camp of kaldorei waits on the shore.

entries.title: Exarch Menelaous
body: The commander of Azure Watch for the Hand of Argus. When the crystals began poisoning the island's nightstalkers, he moved quickly to cull the infected beasts before the corruption could spread through the forests.

entries.title: Admiral Odesyus
body: A human admiral of the Alliance whose flotilla was forced onto Azuremyst's southern shore by goblin saboteurs. He built Odesyus' Landing on the beach, and with the draenei's help discovered that the goblins had a friend among his own crew.

entries.title: Priestess Kyleen Il'dinare
body: A night elf priestess travelling with Admiral Odesyus. Azuremyst was land of her ancestors, and she was grieved to find its ancient ruins tainted by naga.
Like many night elves, she is uneasy around the draenei, who look so much like the eredar of the Burning Legion.

entries.title: Engineer "Spark" Overgrind
body: A gnome engineer of Admiral Odesyus' expedition, and the traitor who betrayed it. He worked for Prince Kael'thas Sunstrider, and through him for the Burning Legion.

entries.title: Cowlen and Magwin
body: A night elf fisherman of Silvermyst Isle and his daughter. When the crash drove the owlkin mad, they and the Siltfin murlocs destroyed Cowlen's home and ship and killed his wife, Thalrisa. He believed his daughter Magwin had died too, but she had survived and was trying to find her way home.

entries.title: Prophet Velen
body: The leader of the draenei since they fled Argus thirteen thousand years before the orcs first came to Azeroth. Velen has the gift of the Sight. When the demon titan Sargeras offered the eredar power, Velen saw the price, refused it, and led the few who would follow him away from their homeworld.

He was once the closest friend of Kil'jaeden, now one of the Burning Legion's greatest lords. Velen has guided his people across the stars ever since, and on Azeroth he pledged them to the Alliance, sensing great courage in it.

entries.title: The Exiled Ones
body: The draenei, whose name means "exiled ones", are eredar who refused the Burning Legion. Led by Velen and guided by the naaru, they fled Argus and wandered the stars for millennia, settling world after world and fleeing each time the demons found them.

At last they settled a world they named Draenor, "exiles' refuge", and lived for centuries in peace with its orcs. Then the Legion found them again. Corrupted by the blood of Mannoroth, the orcs became the Horde and slaughtered the draenei, and the survivors were driven into hiding in a world now called Outland.

entries.title: The Fall of the Exodar
body: The Exodar was built by the naaru as part of Tempest Keep, a dimensional fortress able to cross between worlds. When Kael'thas and his blood elves seized Tempest Keep, the draenei took one of its satellite ships and escaped Outland in it.

They did not escape cleanly. Blood elves of the Sunhawk sabotaged its reactors, and the Exodar crashed into the Azuremyst Isles, breaking apart as it fell. Many died. The survivors, inspired by tales of the Alliance that had stood against the Legion in the Third War, made the wreck their home and pledged themselves to that Alliance.

entries.title: The Crystal Storm
body: When the Exodar broke up, its power crystals rained down across the islands: into lakes, onto beaches, into the caves of the furbolgs. The Stillpine call it the crystal storm.

The crystals leak radiation that mutates the plants and animals that touch them. Lashers and owlkin have been twisted, nightstalkers that swallowed shards carry the sickness through the woods, and old friends among the island's peoples have turned on each other. The draenei have made healing the damage their first task.

entries.title: The Prophecy of Akida
body: Amid the chaos of the crystal storm, an old Stillpine prophecy began to unfold: "A hero will rise, not of furbolg blood, and save the Stillpine tribe."

The Stillpine record their history and prophecies on carved totems, each pointing the way to the next. The draenei learned to read them, and the tribe, led by High Chief Stillpine, became their allies.
